title: Detection of inert arrows by colour projections
statement: Use small quasicategories, coherent triangles and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and symmetric infinity operads and inert maps of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition]. Put $S=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and let $q:Q\to S$ be a symmetric infinity operad. Let $v:a\to b$ lie over an inert pointed map $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$. Choose $q$-cocartesian colour projections $\pi_j:b\to b_j$ over $\rho_j:\langle m\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$, for $1\leq j\leq m$, and coherent composites $\pi_jv$. Then $v$ is $q$-cocartesian if and only if every $\pi_jv$ is $q$-cocartesian. In arity $m=0$ the right-hand condition is empty, so every edge over an inert map to $\langle0\rangle$ is $q$-cocartesian.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Theorem 2.3.3.23(1), printed pp. 266-268; Converse condition (i), Remark 2.1.2.9 and Definition 2.1.1.10: detection of inert arrows by their output projections. Agent expansion of the proof; read online 2026-10-17, WANTED archive in report.md. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.
